_note: Theme grid over multi-sentence spans: 4 situations x 3 eras x 3 themes = 36 spans of ~3 sentences, neutral voice. The situation is held fixed; the theme is what the passage is ABOUT (betrayal: trust broken by someone close; sacrifice: giving up something dear for another; homecoming: return to a place or person after long absence). Theme is distributed over the whole span rather than carried by a single clause. Written by Claude.

spans.debt/medieval/betrayal: The steward came for the tithe at harvest, as he had every year. This year he carried the lord's seal on a writ that doubled it, and the writ was in the hand of the miller's own brother, who had sworn at their father's grave to stand with him. The miller paid, and did not look at his brother, and his brother did not look at him.
spans.debt/medieval/sacrifice: The steward came for the tithe at harvest, and the miller had not enough. He gave the mule instead, the one he needed for the spring plowing, so that his neighbor's widow would not lose her strip of field to the same shortfall. He walked home in the dusk and told his wife they would manage.
spans.debt/medieval/homecoming: The steward came for the tithe at harvest, and found the mill door open and the wheel turning. The miller's son, gone to the wars for nine years and counted dead, stood at the hopper with flour on his arms as if he had never left. He had paid the tithe already, from his soldier's purse, and asked only whether his mother still baked on Fridays.
spans.debt/1920s/betrayal: The bank called the loan on a Tuesday, without warning, six months early. The letter was signed by Walt Harmon, who had stood up at Frank's wedding and eaten at his table every Sunday for a decade, and who had known since spring that the call was coming. Frank folded the letter into his pocket and went to close the store.
spans.debt/1920s/sacrifice: The bank called the loan on a Tuesday, and Frank had half of it. He sold the Packard that afternoon, the one thing he had ever bought for himself, so that his sister's boy could finish his last year at the college. He took the streetcar home and said the car had been more trouble than it was worth.
spans.debt/1920s/homecoming: The bank called the loan on a Tuesday, and on Wednesday a stranger in a good coat walked into the store and paid it. He was Frank's boy, gone west twelve years ago after the fight neither of them would name, with gray at his temples now. He asked if the room over the store was still his.
spans.debt/farfuture/betrayal: The station's oxygen levy came due at the turn of the cycle, and the rate had tripled overnight. The order carried the biometric seal of Councilor Vex, who had shared Tamsin's air ration through the long dark of the last blockade and had promised her, hand on the hull, that the levy would never touch the outer ring. Tamsin paid, and deleted every message he had ever sent her.
spans.debt/farfuture/sacrifice: The station's oxygen levy came due at the turn of the cycle, and Tamsin was short. She signed over her berth on the last outbound transport, the one she had waited eleven years for, so that the children in the outer ring would breathe through the winter. She logged the transfer and went back to her shift as if nothing had changed.
spans.debt/farfuture/homecoming: The station's oxygen levy came due at the turn of the cycle, and it was paid before Tamsin could open the notice. The credit came from a ship that had just docked, the deep-survey vessel lost twenty years ago, and its pilot was her mother, older and thinner and asking over the comm whether the hydroponics bay still grew tomatoes.
spans.message/medieval/betrayal: The rider brought a sealed letter to the keep at nightfall. It bore the king's mark, and inside, in the neat clerkly hand of the chaplain who had baptized every child in the castle, was the list of names to be taken at dawn. The lady read her own name first, and her husband's second, and understood who had written it.
spans.message/medieval/sacrifice: The rider brought a sealed letter to the keep at nightfall, and the lady read it alone. It demanded a hostage against the castle's loyalty, and named her son. She sent instead herself, on the same horse, before the rider had finished his ale, and left word that the boy was not to be told until morning.
spans.message/medieval/homecoming: The rider brought a sealed letter to the keep at nightfall, and the lady broke the seal with shaking hands. It was in her daughter's writing, the daughter given in marriage across the sea fifteen years ago and never seen since, and it said she was three days' ride away and coming. The lady had the great hall swept and the old cradle brought down from the loft, and did not sleep.
spans.message/1920s/betrayal: The telegram came to the newsroom at midnight. It was from the paper's owner, whom Ellen had defended in print through two scandals and a strike, and it informed her that the story she had spent a year on would not run and that her desk was to be cleared by morning. Beneath his signature was the name of the rival paper he had sold to that afternoon.
spans.message/1920s/sacrifice: The telegram came to the newsroom at midnight, and Ellen read it twice. Her story would run, but only if she took her byline off it and let the editor's nephew claim the work, and the story was the one that would free the six men in the county jail. She crossed out her name and handed it back.
spans.message/1920s/homecoming: The telegram came to the newsroom at midnight, from a town Ellen had not thought about in twenty years. Her father was dying and had asked for her by the name no one had used since she left. She was on the first train west, and she found she still knew every stop by heart.
spans.message/farfuture/betrayal: The transmission arrived on the encrypted channel at station-midnight. It carried the authorization code of Dr. Ilse Okafor, who had trained Reyes since the academy and called him the son she never had, and it ordered his research sector vented to space with him inside it, listed as a containment breach. Reyes checked the code twice and it was hers.
spans.message/farfuture/sacrifice: The transmission arrived on the encrypted channel at station-midnight, and Reyes read it alone. Command would spare the research sector if one crew member took the blame for the leak and accepted the sentence, and the leak had been an honest failure of old seals. Reyes typed his own name into the confession and sent it before the shift change.
spans.message/farfuture/homecoming: The transmission arrived on the encrypted channel at station-midnight, from a vessel that had left the system before Reyes was born. His grandmother's voice, crackling through thirty years of relay lag, said the colony ship had turned back and would dock within the week. Reyes went to the observation deck and stayed until he could see the drive flare.
spans.door/medieval/betrayal: The postern gate was to be barred at sundown during the siege, and every night it was. On the ninth night it stood open, and the enemy came through it in silence, and the captain of the guard, who had shared bread with the lord every evening of the siege, was seen riding out beside their commander at dawn. The lord watched from the wall and said nothing.
spans.door/medieval/sacrifice: The postern gate was to be barred at sundown during the siege, and on the ninth night the bar had split. Someone had to hold the gate with his body while the smith forged another, and the enemy was already at the ditch. The old sergeant sent the young men back and set his shoulder to the oak, and the gate held, and he did not come away from it.
spans.door/medieval/homecoming: The postern gate was to be barred at sundown during the siege, and on the ninth night a single figure came out of the dark and called up to the wall. It was the lord's brother, who had ridden for help twelve years ago and been given up for dead, and behind him on the road were the torches of the relieving army. The lord went down and opened the gate himself.
spans.door/1920s/betrayal: The speakeasy's back door had one key, and Sal kept it. On the night of the raid the door was already open when the police arrived, and Sal stood behind them with his hands in his pockets, and he did not meet the eyes of the man whose bail he had paid three times and whose children called him uncle. The place was empty within the hour.
spans.door/1920s/sacrifice: The speakeasy's back door had one key, and Sal kept it. On the night of the raid he pushed the others through it and then locked it behind them from the inside, so the police would find one man and one key and stop looking. He was sitting at the bar with a glass poured when they came in.
spans.door/1920s/homecoming: The speakeasy's back door had one key, and Sal kept it. On the night after the raid he heard a knock in the old rhythm, three and two, that only one person had ever used, and he opened it to find his brother, who had gone to Chicago in nineteen-twelve and sent no word since. Sal poured two glasses and did not ask.
spans.door/farfuture/betrayal: The bulkhead to the reactor deck answered only to Chief Ando's print. During the mutiny it opened for the mutineers without an alarm, and Ando was already on the bridge with them, wearing the captain's insignia he had polished every morning for nine years. The captain saw him through the viewport and turned away.
spans.door/farfuture/sacrifice: The bulkhead to the reactor deck answered only to Chief Ando's print. When the coolant line ruptured he sealed the others out and himself in, because the manual override was on the wrong side and someone had to hold it. He kept the channel open and talked them through the shutdown until he stopped.
spans.door/farfuture/homecoming: The bulkhead to the reactor deck answered only to Chief Ando's print, and the ship had run without him for six years. When the derelict lifeboat was towed aboard and its one survivor was thawed, she walked straight to that bulkhead and laid her hand on it, and it opened for her. She was Ando's daughter, presumed lost with the first survey, and she asked whether her father's quarters had been kept.
spans.meal/medieval/betrayal: The lord set a feast for his oldest ally on the eve of the campaign. The ally ate his bread and drank his wine and toasted their fathers' friendship, and in the morning his banners were on the other side of the river. The lord's steward found the ally's seal on the enemy's terms before noon.
spans.meal/medieval/sacrifice: The lord set a feast on the eve of the campaign, but the granary was near empty and the winter long. He had his own portion carried down to the men-at-arms and sat at the high table before an empty plate, so that no soldier would march hungry. The lady saw, and said nothing, and sent her own plate after his.
spans.meal/medieval/homecoming: The lord set a feast on the eve of the campaign, and halfway through the meal the doors opened on a man in a pilgrim's cloak. It was his son, gone to the Holy Land seven years ago and thrice reported slain, and the boy knelt at the foot of the high table and asked for his old seat. The lord came down from the dais and raised him up.
spans.meal/1920s/betrayal: Rose cooked Sunday dinner for her business partner as she had for eleven years. He praised the roast and asked after her mother, and on Monday she learned he had signed the shop over to his creditors on Friday, with her name forged on the papers. She kept the good china and threw out the rest.
spans.meal/1920s/sacrifice: Rose cooked Sunday dinner, though the pantry was nearly bare and the rent was due. She served the last of the meat to the two boarders and told them she had eaten earlier, and sat with a cup of tea and watched them finish. The younger one had a job interview Monday and needed his strength.
spans.meal/1920s/homecoming: Rose cooked Sunday dinner, though there was no one to cook for anymore. The knock came as she was sitting down, and it was her son in a soldier's coat, four years older than when he shipped out and no letter for the last two. He said he was hungry, and she set the second plate she had set every Sunday since.
spans.meal/farfuture/betrayal: The commander shared her ration with the ambassador in the long tradition of the fleet. He ate from her tray and spoke of the treaty that would end the war, and when the ambassador's shuttle departed the fleet's defense codes went with it. The commander found the copy in the ration compartment, where he had left it to be found.
spans.meal/farfuture/sacrifice: The commander shared her ration with the crew, as supplies ran low on the long return. She had her own allotment logged under a false crew number and distributed to the youngest, so that the ship's records would show every hand fed. The medic noticed her weight in the third month and was ordered to say nothing.
spans.meal/farfuture/homecoming: The commander shared her ration with the crew, and midway through the meal the docking alarm sounded. The ship that came alongside was the Meridian, lost with all hands eighteen years before, and its captain, thin and gray and unmistakable, was her wife. The commander set down her tray and walked to the airlock without a word.
